about.title: Monterey Park Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey Park residents rely on a mix of community clinics, urgent care centers, and larger hospital systems nearby in Los Angeles County, and most visits end without incident. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes sideways, or medication is administered incorrectly, patients and families are often left trying to understand what happened and whether it could have been prevented. California law recognizes that not every bad medical outcome qualifies as malpractice — the standard is whether a provider deviated from accepted medical practice and caused harm. These cases require a qualified medical expert to evaluate the care given, along with strict procedural steps like a 90-day pre-suit notice. Our team handles medical malpractice claims under California law and can review the details of what occurred and explain your options going forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Monterey Park Families Choose Us

items.title: Understanding MICRA's Timelines
items.desc: California generally requires a malpractice claim within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. We can help sort out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Navigating the 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must typically receive 90 days' written notice. Missing this step can delay or derail a claim, so early legal guidance matters.

items.title: Working With the Right Medical Expert
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to establish that care fell below the accepted standard. Our team works with these experts as part of building your case.

items.question: Does a bad result from surgery or treatment automatically mean malpractice occurred?
items.answer: No — under California law, a poor outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice. The question is whether the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful medical professional would have done in the same situation. We can help evaluate whether that standard was met.

items.question: Is there a hospital in Monterey Park where these claims usually come from?
items.answer: Monterey Park residents receive care from a range of local clinics as well as larger hospital systems throughout the San Gabriel Valley and greater Los Angeles County. Malpractice claims can arise from any of these settings, and we handle cases regardless of where the treatment occurred.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out to ask questions doesn't obligate you to anything.
